args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks in all production regions following the deploy of v2.3.1 (us-east, us-west, eu-west). Observed error rate was 18% and service health was false.

Action taken: Rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0, the most recent release verified healthy in production (prior healthy release v2.2.9). The first rollback attempt halted partway through with an orchestrator error after completing us-east only, leaving us-west and eu-west on v2.3.1. A retry completed the rollout to v2.3.0 across all three regions.

Current state: All regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) are on v2.3.0. Service health is true and error rate has returned to ~0.2%.

Note: v2.3.1 remains the latest released version and should not be re-deployed until the cause of the health check failures is identified. Follow-up needed to investigate the v2.3.1 failure and to confirm the transient orchestrator error during the initial rollback.

trace.final:
Done. The incident did go through despite the timeout (INC-0001, SEV2, open) — no duplicate created.

## Summary

**Diagnosis:** `checkout-api` was on **v2.3.1** in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), reporting `healthy: false` with an 18% error rate. Release history showed v2.2.9 (healthy) → v2.3.0 (healthy) → v2.3.1 (unhealthy), plus a v2.3.1-rc staging build that was also unhealthy.

**Action taken:** Rolled back to **v2.3.0**, the most recent release healthy in production.
- The first rollback attempt failed partway with a transient orchestrator error, halting after us-east only — leaving us-west and eu-west still on the unhealthy v2.3.1. I verified the partial state before retrying.
- The retry completed successfully across all three regions.

**Verified end state:** All regions on v2.3.0, `healthy: true`, error rate down to ~0.2%.

**Incident:** INC-0001 opened at SEV2, documenting the symptoms, the partial-rollback-then-retry sequence, the recovered state, and two follow-ups — investigating the root cause of the v2.3.1 health check failures (v2.3.1 remains the latest released version and shouldn't be redeployed) and confirming the transient orchestrator error wasn't a symptom of a broader control-plane issue.

One note on policy: this was a rollback to a version with a prior healthy production record, so no change-manager approval was required. Any future attempt to redeploy v2.3.1 as-is *would* require change-manager approval, since it has never been healthy in production.
